conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: TYPE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'The description of any data item subordinate to type-name-1 shall not contain a SAME AS clause that references the subject of this entry or any group item to which this entry is subordinate.' No TYPE-side screen is written for SR1; it is enforced through the SAME AS expansion's §13.18.49.3 SR3 ancestor walk, which runs over the TYPE clone (the clone makes the SAME AS entry subordinate to the TYPE subject, so SR1's two referents are exactly SR3's). Probes: `01 T TYPEDEF. 05 A SAME AS REC.` + `01 REC. 05 X TYPE T.` -> COBOLNET1557; `05 A SAME AS Y` + `01 Y TYPE T.` (the subject itself) -> COBOLNET1557; grandparent through two levels -> COBOLNET1557; legal control (SAME AS an unrelated item) compiles and DISPLAY Y prints 'WXYZ12'. Same verdict at --std 2002. The diagnostic cites §13.18.49.3 SR3 rather than §13.18.57.3 SR1 and says 'a group item' even for the subject-itself case — a labeling nuance, not a wrong verdict. No spec-derived test targets the TYPE-side shape; test-needed. cite.py --check 13.18.57.3 and 13.18.49.3 SR3 text OK. probes under out13/probe/type-clause-p1/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe, --std 2023 unless noted) || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): Format 1: COBOL-2002, 2014, 2023 (the TYPEDEF/TYPE family; absent from COBOL-85; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to §13.18.57). Not edition-gated beyond the clause's own introduction gate.
rows.rule-text: The description of any data item subordinate to type-name-1 shall not contain a SAME AS clause that references the subject of this entry or any group item to which this entry is subordinate.

rows.subject: TYPE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'RH is an abbreviation for REPORT HEADING. ... RF is an abbreviation for REPORT FOOTING.' reportGroupType pairs each full spelling with its abbreviation as one alternative; GroupKindOf maps both to the same ReportGroupKindModel. Probe fmt_abbrev_all (RH/PH/CH/DE/CF/PF/RF) and fmt_fullwords_all (all full spellings) compile and print the identical report. cite.py --check 13.18.57.3 'RH is an abbreviation for REPORT HEADING.' OK. No spec-derived test pinning the equivalence located. probes under out13/probe/type-clause-p1/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe, --std 2023) || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): Format 2 (report writer): COBOL-85 optional Report Writer module; ISO 2023 optional language element A.4.11; 2002/2014 availability not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d); Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to the TYPE clause
rows.rule-text: RH is an abbreviation for REPORT HEADING. PH is an abbreviation for PAGE HEADING. CH is an abbreviation for CONTROL HEADING. DE is an abbreviation for DETAIL. CF is an abbreviation for CONTROL FOOTING. PF is an abbreviation for PAGE FOOTING. RF is an abbreviation for REPORT FOOTING.

rows.subject: TYPE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'Following CONTROL HEADING or CONTROL FOOTING, data-name-1, data-name-2, or FINAL may be omitted only if the CONTROL clause ... contains exactly one operand.' ResolveReports: omitted operand -> ControlLevel = Controls.Count == 1 ? 0 : -1, -1 draws COBOLNET0899 report-control-type-operand. Probes: CONTROL IS CX CY + `TYPE CH` -> rejected; CONTROL IS FINAL CX + `TYPE CF` -> rejected (FINAL counts as an operand); no CONTROL clause + `TYPE CF` -> rejected; CONTROL IS CX + `TYPE CONTROL FOOTING` -> runs, CF prints at TERMINATE; CONTROL IS FINAL + `TYPE CF` -> runs. Both halves verified. Positive half is exercised incidentally by conformance:2023/rw_suppress (TYPE CH with one-operand CONTROL) but no test targets the rejection half; test-needed. cite.py --check OK. probes under out13/probe/type-clause-p1/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe, --std 2023) || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): Format 2 (report writer): COBOL-85 optional Report Writer module; ISO 2023 optional language element A.4.11; 2002/2014 availability not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d); Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to the TYPE clause (whether COBOL-85 permitted the omission at all is not derivable from the 2023 text; the code does not gate it)
rows.rule-text: Following CONTROL HEADING or CONTROL FOOTING, data-name-1, data-name-2, or FINAL may be omitted only if the CONTROL clause in the corresponding report description entry contains exactly one operand.

rows.subject: TYPE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'If no GENERATE data-name statements are specified in the procedure division, the report description need not contain a DETAIL.' A permission: no code demands a DETAIL. Probe sr16_no_detail_ok (CONTROL IS CX, only TYPE CF CX, GENERATE R1) compiles and prints the footing 'FFF' at TERMINATE. The converse (GENERATE data-name naming a non-DETAIL) is rejected by §14.9.16.3 SR1 (probe sr16_gen_dataname_no_detail), which is GENERATE's rule, not this one. cite.py --check OK. probes under out13/probe/type-clause-p1/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe, --std 2023) || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): Format 2 (report writer): COBOL-85 optional Report Writer module; ISO 2023 optional language element A.4.11; 2002/2014 availability not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d); Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to the TYPE clause
rows.rule-text: If no GENERATE data-name statements are specified in the procedure division, the report description need not contain a DETAIL.

rows.subject: TYPE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.18.57.4 "level-numbers in the resulting hierarchy may exceed 49" -> OK; "the subject of the entry is aligned as though it were a level 1 item" -> OK). a) CloneItem reproduces each subordinate with its name, full entry description (CopyEntryDescription scope Entry), OCCURS, REDEFINES, INDEXED BY and 88s, recursively -> same names/descriptions/hierarchy (probe t1: C OF B OF X addressable, qualified). b)/c) the hierarchy is carried structurally (Parent/Children), and TYPE passes levelDelta 0 (level-verbatim clone); nothing downstream reads a clone's level-number for hierarchy, so the 'adjusted if necessary' effect holds: probe t6 (E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out13/probe/type-clause-p2/t6.cob) places a group TYPE subject at level 49 (children written 05/10) and composes ACC / C OF X = CC / LENGTH(B OF X) = 2, i.e. the result hierarchy below level 49 is accepted, as GR2c permits. d) alignment: this compiler inserts no slack bytes for SYNCHRONIZED (probe t7: a TYPEDEF with `05 A PIC X. 05 B BINARY-LONG SYNC.` measures 5 both as an 01 and as an 05 subject, and the identical inline group measures 5) -- alignment/slack is implementor-defined (13.18.55), so 'aligned as though it were a level 1 item' has no observable divergence; the TypeSubject scope withholds the template entry's own SYNC/ALIGNED, consistent with GR1's alignment exclusion. No existing spec-derived golden exercises a non-level-1 group subject's renumbering (typedef_weak_group covers a) at level 1 only), so test-ref is empty. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (TYPE Format 1 / TYPEDEF family is a COBOL-2002 introduction per the project's constructs row type-clause-2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to 13.18.57.4 Format 1)
rows.rule-text: If type-name-1 describes a group item: a) the subject of the entry is a group whose subordinate elements have the same names, descriptions, and hierarchy as the subordinate elements of type-name-1, b) the level-numbers of items subordinate to that group are adjusted, if necessary, to preserve the hierarchy of type-name-1, c) level-numbers in the resulting hierarchy may exceed 49, d) the subject of the entry is aligned as though it were a level 1 item.

rows.subject: TYPE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.18.57.4 "that BASED clause applies and any BASED clause specified in the description of type-name-1 is ignored for this entry" -> OK). Both halves hold: the subject's own BASED is set at BindEntry (item.IsBased = isBased) and is never overwritten by the copy (IsBased is DescriptionCopyKind.None); probe t3 (E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out13/probe/type-clause-p2/t3.cob): `01 T TYPEDEF PIC X(5). 01 X TYPE T BASED. ... SET ADDRESS OF X TO ADDRESS OF Y. DISPLAY X.` -> HELLO, correct. The template's BASED is ignored for such an entry (never copied). NOTE the same None classification is WRONG for the complementary case the rule does not govern -- a subject WITHOUT its own BASED over a BASED template must become based under GR1 / 13.18.58.4 GR3; that divergence is recorded on GR-13.18.57.4-1, not here. pb513_type_entry_composition writes BASED beside TYPE but never references the item, so it does not observe 'applies'; test-ref empty. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (TYPE Format 1 / TYPEDEF family is a COBOL-2002 introduction per the project's constructs row type-clause-2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to 13.18.57.4 Format 1)
rows.rule-text: If a BASED clause is specified in the data description of the subject of the entry, that BASED clause applies and any BASED clause specified in the description of type-name-1 is ignored for this entry.

rows.subject: TYPEDEF clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.58.3 "If the TYPEDEF clause is specified with the EXTERNAL clause, the type declaration shall be at level-number 1" OK. The compiler confines EVERY TYPEDEF to level 1 (§13.16.3 SR15, --check OK), which subsumes this rule: probe td10extsub ('01 G. 05 T TYPEDEF EXTERNAL PIC X.') -> COBOLNET1529; level-1 TYPEDEF EXTERNAL accepted (td15extnote, td22nois); TYPEDEF STRONG EXTERNAL accepted at 2023 and COBOLNET0900 at 2002/2014 (td21strongext). conformance:negative/pb488-typedef-subordinate covers a subordinate TYPEDEF WITHOUT EXTERNAL, so it does not witness this rule's combination; test-ref empty. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (STRONG with EXTERNAL only from 2023: E.3.3 item 20, --check OK "External data items may now be strongly typed"; gated by VersionConformancePass.VisitExternalClause)
rows.rule-text: If the TYPEDEF clause is specified with the EXTERNAL clause, the type declaration shall be at level-number 1.

rows.subject: TYPEDEF clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.58.4 "A type declaration has no storage associated with it" OK. A TYPEDEF root is registered in TypeDecls and never added to _roots/newRoots (the storage emitter's source) nor to ByName. Probe td06storage ('01 T TYPEDEF PIC X(5).' MOVE "A" TO T) -> COBOLNET1639 'T' is not defined: the type-name is not a storage-bearing item. td06len FUNCTION LENGTH(T) = 5 is correct and not storage: §15.50.3 rule 1 (--check OK) admits a type-name as argument-1. No spec-derived test asserts the absence of storage; test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: A type declaration has no storage associated with it.

rows.subject: Types
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.5.3.1 'Currency symbols match if and only if the corresponding currency strings are the same' -> OK §8.5.3.1 1)). Code: PictureAnalyzer canonicalizes every currency SYMBOL in the mask to '$' and records the currency STRING in PicInfo.CurrencyString (null when the string is '$'); StrongTypeModel.SameAnalyzedProfile compares the PicInfo record (canonical EditMask + CurrencyString), so the match is by string, not by symbol - exactly the rule. The only cross-configuration site is two SEPARATE outermost source elements (§12.3.7.4 GR1 makes a contained unit inherit the container's currency signs), reached through a program-prototype CALL whose strongly-typed formal runs OoConformance.StrongTypeMismatch -> StrongTypeModel.SameType. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\types): TPD caller default currency 'PIC $$9' vs callee CURRENCY SIGN IS "$" WITH PICTURE SYMBOL "U" 'PIC UU9' (different symbols, same string) -> compiles and runs 'OK' (expected: match, conforms); TPE caller '$'->"$" vs callee CURRENCY SIGN IS "#" WITH PICTURE SYMBOL "$" both 'PIC $$9' (same symbol, different strings) -> COBOLNET1688 strongly-typed argument not of the same type (expected: no match, conforms). Both directions verified. No existing spec-derived test exercises the currency exception (grep of tests/ for TYPEDEF together with CURRENCY SIGN finds none) -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.5.3.1 types: TYPEDEF/TYPE/STRONG exist from 2002; the ALIGNED item of the clause list is a 2023 change per Annex E.2 item 2; the LOCALE-phrase half applies only where PICTURE format 2 (§13.18.40.2) exists - Annex E of the 2023 text does not date that phrase)]
rows.rule-text: Currency symbols match if and only if the corresponding currency strings are the same.
